author: Mark Atwood
text:
PARTLY ANSWERED by bead mimid-75nk.14, and nobody had linked the two.
Both observations are from 2026-11-22 and they disagree, because they are
different deployments:

- THIS bead, our own copy of mimi-hubd at 34eae7e: no client certificate
  -> the handshake itself fails. It REQUIRES one.
- mimid-75nk.14, Jason's PUBLIC hub: signature only -> HTTP 200, handle
  resolved, and exactly one CertificateRequest in the handshake. It ASKS
  but does not require one.

So the open question here -- "Check his before the interop day" -- has a
data point: as of 2026-11-22 his public hub did not require a client
certificate, and mimid can reach it on signatures alone. That removes the
"moves from optional to required" worry for his hub, and leaves it as a
fact about our copy at 34eae7e rather than about Haven generally. Either
he runs a different revision or a different TLS configuration; which, we
do not know and have not asked.

What this does NOT change: the diagnosability complaint above stands for
the requiring mode, and selftest.sh accepting either shape was the right
call, since we now have both shapes in the wild on the same day.

NOT A HAVEN BUG, either half, and ruling that out is bead mimid-7yn7.9's
rule. Rejecting an untrusted client certificate when one is offered is
what a mainstream TLS stack does: the fake peer in
crates/mimid-server/tests/peer_client_tls.rs is rustls with
WebPkiClientVerifier::builder(...).allow_unauthenticated(), which is the
standard "request but do not require" mode, and it answers an untrusted
certificate with the identical AlertReceived(UnknownCA). Our own library
behaves as Jason's hub did. The bug in that episode was mimid's, and it
is fixed in d909bb1b.
